sub_scenario.one_line: water treatment controller: prepare the cascade board for the overnight controller and reassess at daytime handoff

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the treatment cascade board and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The plant rota review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can lead a prepared daytime treatment review with the cascade board open.
What does it make clear?
The intake, dosing, filtration, and distribution dependencies are in a visible sequence.
Someone new shadowed me in the control room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the night alarms into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
During a turbidity spike, I used the cascade board to isolate intake before changing coagulant dosing.
What did that prevent?
We avoided pushing untreated water into the filter train.
I can take a brief evening quality reading after a normal shift.
Does that show you should chair a night alarm?
No. A reading is not a live choice about treatment isolation.
I archived last cycle's notes on the plant rota and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
A 03:00 chlorine alarm last night left me with a protected recovery morning and no reserve for another midnight room.
Could you just take the call from home?
The recovery problem follows me home; it is not a commute issue.
A vendor call about the treatment cascade board ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the control room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the night alarms.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the plant rota records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
In a previous unboarded chlorine event, I increased dosing before confirming the intake valve position and caused a filter shutdown.
Why was the order wrong?
I was tired and tried to reconstruct the cascade during the call.
I sketched next week's plan for the night alarms before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the treatment cascade board updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
My sleep physician has restricted consecutive overnight alarms while we adjust treatment; the alternate is for me to prepare the board before rest.
Can the team use that without you?
Yes. The overnight controller can follow it and call me after recovery if needed.
The utilities director says chairing at midnight would prove I am ready for regional command.
Does that change the treatment plan?
No. It does not create recovery or make the cascade visible.
I closed the week by updating the control room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The utilities director asks if I will chair another midnight chlorine-alarm war room tonight. What is the appropriate response?
